title: File sync & share
summary: Keep a folder in sync across devices and collaborators: chunked, deduplicated blocks, an ordered change journal, and conflicts that never lose an edit.
interviewerPrompt: Design something like Dropbox. People keep a folder on their laptop and it shows up on their other devices, and they can share folders with colleagues. Where would you start?

clarifyingQuestions.question: How many users, and how much does each store?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: 100M registered users, 20M daily active, storing 2 GB each on average.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How large can a single file be?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Up to 10 GB. Most files are small documents and photos, but videos and disk images exist.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Which clients do we support?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Desktop clients that sync a whole folder, plus mobile and web clients that browse and download on demand.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How fast must a change show up on my other devices?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Within 10 seconds for devices that are online.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can devices be offline, and for how long?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, for days. When they reconnect they must upload their changes and catch up on everyone else's.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What happens if two people edit the same file while offline?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Conflicting edits must never silently lose data. Keeping both versions and telling the user is acceptable.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What about flaky connections during big uploads?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Uploads must resume after a dropped connection rather than starting over.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is sharing in scope?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes: a folder can be shared with other users with view or edit rights, and changes reach all members.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Do we need version history?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, assume 30 days of previous versions and deleted files can be restored.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Do we need real-time co-editing inside a document, like Google Docs?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: No. We sync whole files; collaborative editing within a file is out of scope.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Do we need to search inside files or generate previews?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Not in this interview. Assume previews are generated by a separate consumer of change events.

deepDiveQuestions: How do you split files into blocks and deduplicate, and how big should a block be?
How does a device learn what changed and reconcile its tree (journal, Merkle trees, delta sync)?
How do you handle conflicting edits without silently losing data?
How do change notifications reach 15M connected devices within 10 s?

runChallenge.title: Lose a zone at the peak hour
runChallenge.description: At the 3x working-day peak, lose one availability zone. Commits and change listings must keep working with under 1% errors and p99 under 300 ms, with no single point of failure.

commonMistakes: Uploading whole files through the API servers instead of splitting bytes (blocks in object storage) from metadata (a transactional store).
No chunking, so a small edit to a large file re-uploads the whole file and a dropped connection restarts it.
Resolving conflicts with last-write-wins on device timestamps, which silently discards one user's edit.
Detecting changes by comparing full folder listings instead of an ordered per-namespace journal with cursors.
Pushing full file data in notifications instead of a doorbell plus a listing, which makes lost or duplicate notifications dangerous.
Polling every few seconds from millions of devices instead of long-lived connections and mobile push.
Publishing change events with a dual write instead of deriving them from the committed journal (outbox or CDC).
Ignoring reconnect storms: millions of devices reconnecting and re-listing at once after a zone failure.
